discussion_comments.comment_body: We should check the node type instead of accessing non-existing properties.
Done — branches on node type now, and only treats a DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE as a root when it has a host, same as scrollIntoView below.

We can use `getOwnerDocumentFromRootContainer` [like we do for blur](https://github.com/scs0209/react/blob/f3df1254727f641b7403bd77d3104d8a15e66cb1/packages/react-dom-bindings/src/client/ReactFiberConfigDOM.js#L3329-L3332)
Good call — updated to use `getOwnerDocumentFromRootContainer` here as well.
why not copy it from the other callsite verbatim?
You're right — I overcomplicated the cast. Updated to match the blur callsite.
Should we split the `InitializationHandler` type up into an errored and "normal" version to narrow down its `reason`?

Yes, done. The four places that flip a handler cast to `ErroredInitializationHandler` before writing, like the chunk transitions do. The refinements fall out: `handler.reason` is `mixed` inside the `errored` branches and `null | FlightStreamController` after the guard in `initializeChunkIfUnblocked`, so the typed `initializeBlockedChunk` parameter is now checked.

There is a chance you might end up receiving `TypeError`: calling `displayName.startsWith(...)` if `this.showNames` is `false`.

Thank for pointing that out. I’ve updated the code to avoid the potential TypeError by ensuring `displayName` is only processed when `showNames` is true.

I also revamped the display name parsing logic to make it more extensible. As part of this, I added a 🧠 icon for components wrapped in `React.Memo`, and display names are now consistently unwrapped from HOCs for better clarity. Let me know if there’s anything else!

We already guarded at runtime that `null` can't be passed in here as parent.

`div == null`

Please learn about the difference between `== null` and `=== null`
Why? I think the types are correct here, `div` can't be `undefined`. Otherwise Flow would raise an error here.

I'd not rely on flow here and expand the range of negatives we check for to either `div == null` or `!div`.
The fact that it could only be either null or an element feels like being in the implementation details category for me. The code just reads better when it says "if there's no diff" and not "if diff is not null".
Also there's no performance hit to do that, it covers more edge cases, and it's type safe.
